title: Lopburi Old Town Street Food 2026 — Eat Before the Palaces | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A walking food guide to Lopburi's old town in Thailand: classic rice-and-curry shops, beef noodles by Narai Palace, plus street snacks at Sa Kaeo market and the night market by the train station — all at real local prices.
keywords: Lopburi food, Lopburi street food, Lopburi old town, Lopburi rice and curry, Sa Kaeo market Lopburi
intro: You can wander Lopburi on foot all day — Narai Palace, the Phra Prang Sam Yot ruins, and Vichayen House all sit within walking distance of each other. But the thing many people forget to plan is the meals in between. Lopburi's old town is packed with long-running rice-and-curry shops, thirty-year-old beef noodle stalls, and street snacks in markets where prices are still what locals pay. We've mapped out a walking food route for you, from breakfast before the palace to evening sweets at the night market.

blocks.html: The nice thing about Lopburi is that everything clusters into one neighborhood. From Lopburi train station it's just a few minutes' walk to Phra Prang Sam Yot, and a little further on you reach Narai Ratchaniwet Palace. Along the way, rice-and-curry shops, noodle stalls, and street carts pop up the whole route. The trick is to eat a little at several places rather than filling up at one — that way you get to try the most local dishes.

blocks.text: Old-School Curry and Savory Shops in the Old Town

blocks.html: Rice and curry (khao gaeng) is the heart of lunch for people in Lopburi, and prices still start in the double digits in baht — two scoops over rice and you're full. Beef noodles near the palace are another local favorite, the kind visitors to Narai Palace usually stop for before or after their walk.

items.name: Khao Gaeng Thot Suea
items.blurb: A long-established curry-rice shop that everyone in Lopburi knows. The name (literally "shirt-off curry rice") comes from the old days when the owner liked to sit out front shirtless while selling. What keeps people coming back is the chili pastes, pounded fresh for every bowl with real depth of flavor — especially the shrimp-paste-and-mackerel nam phrik eaten with fresh veggies. It's a homely, filling lunch that won't cost much.

items.name: Beef Noodles, Song Shop (Phraya Kamjat Rd, by Narai Palace)
items.blurb: A Lopburi beef-noodle institution, sitting on Phraya Kamjat Road right in front of Narai Ratchaniwet Palace. It's been going for more than thirty years — a rich, well-balanced beef broth and tender meat. Perfect for a stop before or after walking the palace, since it's right against the palace wall.

items.name: Buffet Curry Rice, Krua Mae Rabiap
items.blurb: Curry rice buffet-style — scoop as much as you want for one flat price. Good if you're really hungry or you've come as a group and want to try a bit of everything. The dishes rotate like a Thai home kitchen: red curry, stir-fried veg, fried things, all on one plate.

items.name: Late-Night Curry Rice, Old Town Area
items.blurb: For anyone arriving in Lopburi late or wandering into the evening, the old town has curry shops that stay open late. The dishes are still hot, so you can grab a plate over rice before heading back to your room. Prices are still the local kind.

items.name: Khao Man Gai / Khao Kha Moo, Sa Kaeo Night Market
items.blurb: Inside Sa Kaeo night market there's a regular Hainanese chicken rice and stewed pork leg over rice stall that locals queue for. A quick, filling one-plate meal — good for dinner before you move on to dessert in the same market.

blocks.title: A Tip About the Monkeys
blocks.html: The Phra Prang Sam Yot area and around the Kala Shrine are full of monkeys. Don't carry a food bag or plastic bag walking through that zone — the monkeys will grab it. If you want to eat street food, move over toward Sa Kaeo market or in front of the train station, where the monkeys don't come down. You'll eat in peace there.

blocks.text: Street Snacks — Eat as You Go

blocks.html: This is the fun part. Lopburi's street food spreads across the upper market, the lower market, the city shrine, and Sa Kaeo market. Most are long-running carts run by the same families for years, and a skewer or a bag costs just a few baht. Graze your way along and you can try plenty for under ฿100.

items: Mini Patongko with Sangkhaya (Upper Market) — little Chinese doughnuts fried fresh, dipped in sangkhaya custard. A morning snack that goes well with coffee.
Grilled Sticky Rice (Upper Market) — fragrant off the grill, with taro, custard, or banana filling, just a few baht a skewer. Easy to carry and eat on the walk to the palace.
Som Fak Somporn (Lower Market) — a sour-salty local specialty eaten with ginger and peanuts, a light edible souvenir that Lopburi folks have eaten for ages.
Pa Yai Fried Sausage (City Shrine) — the regular fried-sausage stall in front of the city shrine, served hot with spicy jaew dipping sauce.
Pa Ta Fried Meatballs (Rachanusorn Park) — crisp outside, soft inside, near the public park — easy snacking on a stroll.
Lung Khiao's Tokyo Snacks (in front of Sa Kaeo bus terminal) — an old-school spot for savory and sweet Tokyo rolls, rolled fresh each time, at genuine street-food prices.

blocks.text: Sa Kaeo Night Market — Dinner Through to Dessert

blocks.html: Sa Kaeo night market sits near the Sa Kaeo roundabout and is where locals come for dinner. It's packed with both savory and sweet — chicken rice, stewed pork leg, khanom jeen, pork satay, fried chicken, soy milk, and fruit smoothies. Prices are still local, and you can knock out a whole meal in one spot.

items.name: Chrysanthemum Slushie, Rattanacharoensap
items.blurb: Chrysanthemum tea blended into a slushie, sweet at just the right level — a cold cup to cool down after a full day of walking the market.

items.name: Durian over Coconut Ice Cream (Chok Nakin)
items.blurb: Fresh coconut ice cream topped with durian, the kind of cool dessert people queue for in Sa Kaeo market.

items.name: Khun Yai Toi Sweets Shop
items.blurb: Thai sweets made fresh and well-balanced — good for finishing a meal or taking back to your room.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: Sa Kaeo night market gets busy from evening into the night. Arrive a bit before dark and you'll catch everything while the stalls are still open. Popular sweets like the durian-coconut ice cream tend to sell out fast on weekends.

blocks.text: Night Market by the Train Station + Phraya Kamjat Walking Street

blocks.html: If you come to Lopburi by train (a popular choice since it's an easy ride out of Bangkok), you'll hit the night market right by the train station the moment you step off. Prices are standard and affordable, so you can grab something to eat before checking in.

items: Amataros Roti (railway night market) — roti crisp outside and soft inside, made fresh, a popular snack by the station.
Hi-Tech Bua Loi (in front of Hor congee shop, railway night market) — bua loi in hot ginger syrup to finish a meal, good for a cool evening.
Cho Salapao (Route 2 road) — hot steamed buns with hearty fillings, easy to carry onto the train for the ride.
Cho Home-Style Grilled Chicken (Narai roundabout) — the regular grilled-chicken stall; take it back to your room to eat with sticky rice.

blocks.html: And if you happen to be there on a Wednesday, don't miss the Phraya Kamjat walking street, which only opens on Wednesdays. It's in the Tha Hin area in front of Narai Palace, with street food and local goods lined up the whole way — a great chance to graze your way through a genuine local market.

blocks.text: A Café to Rest Your Legs with an Old-Town View

blocks.html: Walking the temples and palace under the Lopburi sun gets pretty hot, so it helps to have a café to rest your legs before moving on.

items.name: Nom-Cup-D
items.blurb: A café right across from Narai Ratchaniwet Palace, where you can sip coffee looking at the old palace wall. There are Thai sweets to go with it — a good spot to rest mid-walk.

faq.q: What should I eat in Lopburi's old town?
faq.a: The standouts are old-school curry rice like Khao Gaeng Thot Suea, and the beef noodles at Song shop in front of Narai Palace. For street food, head to Sa Kaeo market and the night market by the train station, where there's both savory and sweet at local prices.

faq.q: Roughly how much does food in Lopburi cost?
faq.a: It's still local pricing. Curry over rice starts around ฿40–60, beef noodles around ฿50–70, and street snacks like grilled sticky rice, fried sausage, and Tokyo rolls run just a few baht a skewer or bag. You can graze through plenty for under ฿100.

faq.q: Should I eat before or after visiting Narai Palace?
faq.a: The Song beef-noodle shop is on Phraya Kamjat Road right by the palace, so it's easy to stop before or after your walk. Curry rice is best for lunch, and save Sa Kaeo market for dinner through to dessert.

faq.q: How do I avoid the monkeys while eating street food?
faq.a: The Phra Prang Sam Yot zone and the Kala Shrine have lots of monkeys — don't carry a food bag or plastic bag through there, as the monkeys will grab it. If you want to eat while walking, move over to Sa Kaeo market or in front of the train station, where the monkeys don't come down.

faq.q: Is it easy to find food if I come to Lopburi by train?
faq.a: Yes. As soon as you step off, the night market by the train station is right there with plenty of food at standard prices, and it's a short walk from the station to Phra Prang Sam Yot and Narai Palace.
